title: Gemcitabine alone · non-small-cell lung cancer
purpose: Gemcitabine aims to control lung cancer and its symptoms. Treatment is reviewed against side effects, your health and your priorities; benefit is not guaranteed.

agents.name: Gemcitabine
agents.explanation: Gemcitabine interferes with making DNA, which dividing cancer cells need. Healthy blood-forming cells and other tissues can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report fever, unusual bleeding, breathlessness, rash, swelling or reduced urine promptly.
risks: Rare serious lung or kidney injury

phases.label: Repeated 28 day cycles
phases.detail: Gemcitabine is given on Days 1, 8 and 15. Week 4 has no planned dose. Each cycle lasts 28 days. For lung cancer there is no fixed six-cycle limit in this source: continue only while the team considers treatment helpful and tolerable.

phases.label: Review benefit and recovery
phases.detail: Your team decides when to scan and whether to continue, pause or change treatment. Surgery and radiotherapy are separate plans.

timeline.label: Symptom awareness
timeline.text: Symptoms may occur on any day; this is not a personal risk curve.

support.title: Sickness medicines
support.text: Gemcitabine has low sickness risk. Follow the prescribed preventive or rescue medicine plan; do not take a platinum anti-sickness course for gemcitabine alone.

support.title: Feeling unwell
support.text: Do not dismiss fever as a flu-like drug effect. Call the oncology team immediately for fever, shaking chills or sudden illness.

support.title: Medicines and fluids
support.text: Follow your individual drinking advice. Report reduced urine, swelling, breathlessness or trouble drinking, and ask before new medicines or supplements.

questions.a: The same medicine is planned on Days 1, 8 and 15, followed by a week without a planned dose. Each visit has its own safety checks.

evidence.intro: Gemcitabine has been studied in older adults with advanced lung cancer.
evidence.interpretation: Small historical single-arm older-adult study cannot establish a comparative survival benefit or predict an individual outcome.
evidence.title: Understanding the evidence

context_label: Locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC in older adults or people with ECOG2
indication_text: NCCP 00284b: elderly patients or patients with ECOG2 with locally advanced/metastatic NSCLC.
schedule_summary: Gemcitabine is given on Days 1, 8 and 15. Week 4 has no planned dose. Each cycle lasts 28 days. For lung cancer there is no fixed six-cycle limit in this source: continue only while the team considers treatment helpful and tolerable.
administration_text: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² is infused over 30 minutes on Days 1, 8 and 15. The complete visit takes longer for blood results, review, pharmacy preparation and prescribed support.
monitoring_summary: Blood count before every dose; kidney and liver tests before each cycle. Baseline blood count, kidney and liver tests are required. Hearing tests and a measured/estimated kidney-clearance assessment are arranged when clinically indicated.

monitoring_schedule.title: My tests and checks
monitoring_schedule.note: Required safety checks are distinct from individual response imaging and follow-up. No routine tumour-marker interval is specified.

urgent_extra: Call oncology immediately for fever or sudden illness, breathing difficulty, chest pain, uncontrolled vomiting, bleeding, very little urine, severe headache or confusion, or a spreading/blistering rash. Tell the nurse about infusion-site pain.
consent_support: Discuss blood-count suppression and serious infection, bleeding, nausea, fatigue, skin reactions, rare serious lung/kidney effects, fertility and individual alternatives.

sections.title: Before each visit
sections.text: Bring your medicine list and report illness. The team reviews blood results before deciding the dose.

sections.title: Three treatment visits
sections.text: Day 1,Day 8 and Day 15 are planned infusion visits. Week 4 has no routine dose.

sections.title: At home
sections.text: Keep the prescribed support medicines and urgent contact plan available. Do not make up a missed dose yourself.

anatomy: Urgent advice for severe headache, confusion, seizures or vision change.
New or worsening breathlessness needs urgent advice.
Report mouth sores, vomiting or trouble drinking.
Call for much less urine, swelling or sudden illness.
A spreading rash, blisters or peeling skin needs urgent review.
Fever, infection symptoms or unusual bleeding need prompt advice.

chronology_notes.title: Timing varies
chronology_notes.text: Tiredness, bowel changes and infection can occur between visits. Blood tests and your symptoms guide dose decisions; there is no guaranteed safe day.

chronology_notes.title: Changes to the plan
chronology_notes.text: The team may delay, omit or reduce doses for safety. Do not add a missed dose yourself.

timeline_note: Relative treatment days, without personal dates. Symptoms are not confined to a fixed day.
safety_note: Call oncology immediately for fever or sudden illness, breathing difficulty, chest pain, uncontrolled vomiting, bleeding, very little urine, severe headache or confusion, or a spreading/blistering rash. Tell the nurse about infusion-site pain.
passport_visit_note: Use another record for each new cycle. Record actual dose dates and omitted doses; the record is not a fixed course-length target.
